sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: maxUnavailable and maxSurge (defaults 25%), kubectl rollout status and history, and kubectl rollout undo --to-revision, with revision history kept in old ReplicaSets.

Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: helm rollback takes a release name and a revision and rolls the release back to that revision, with --wait, --timeout and --cleanup-on-fail.

Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: --atomic rolls back the changes of a failed upgrade and turns on --wait, which waits until Pods and Deployments are ready, up to --timeout (default 5m0s).

The company, the cluster, the applications and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You are the developer on call for the store front at Pebblebrook Toys, a fictional toy retailer. A release of the catalog service went out at 14:50. Half the catalog Pods are not ready, and the search team's Helm upgrade failed half-way an hour ago.
handover: catalog Deployment: strategy RollingUpdate with maxUnavailable 100% and maxSurge 0 (copied from a batch job's manifest).
search: Helm release revision 7 failed during upgrade; revision 6 was healthy.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the map shows each component and its status in words.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Check-in 2: the laptop's manifest is two releases old; the catalog comes back with last month's prices on 300 products.
Check-in 3: the fix rolls out with Recreate; the catalog is down for 90 seconds during the after-school peak.
Check-in 4: the uninstall removed the search index's volume claim; search is down for three hours while the index rebuilds.

effects.log: Check-in 2: the fix is ready to release again.
Check-in 3: the search team asks for help.

undoPrompt.title: No catalog Pods available
undoPrompt.context: Revision 11 was healthy; revision 12 lacks a config key.

choices.label: kubectl rollout undo deploy/catalog to revision 11, watch rollout status until 6/6 are available, then fix the config key before re-releasing
choices.feedback: rollout undo returns the Deployment to a known-good revision; rollout status confirms it.

choices.label: Add the missing key to the ConfigMap and restart the new Pods

effects.log: The key is added; the new Pods restart.

choices.feedback: It works, but the catalog stays down while you find and fix the key.

choices.label: Delete the Deployment and apply the old manifest from your laptop

effects.log: The Deployment is deleted and re-created.

choices.feedback: Deleting loses the rollout history, and your laptop's copy is two releases old.

stratPrompt.title: maxUnavailable 100%
stratPrompt.context: The strategy removes every old Pod before new ones are ready.

choices.label: Set maxUnavailable 0 and maxSurge 25%, so new Pods must be ready before old ones go, and release the fix

effects.log: The fix rolls out with no drop in capacity.

choices.feedback: With maxUnavailable 0 a rollout never removes a serving Pod until its replacement is ready.

choices.label: Set maxUnavailable 50%

effects.log: Half the Pods may be unavailable.

choices.feedback: Better than 100%, but a bad release still halves capacity at the peak.

choices.label: Switch to the Recreate strategy so versions never mix
choices.feedback: Recreate stops every old Pod before starting new ones: every release is an outage.

helmfixPrompt.title: A half-applied upgrade
helmfixPrompt.context: Revision 7 failed part-way; revision 6 was healthy.

choices.label: helm rollback search 6, confirm with helm history and the Pods, and use --atomic with a timeout for the next upgrade

effects.log: The release is back on revision 6's configuration; helm history shows the rollback and search is healthy.

choices.feedback: helm rollback restores a known revision as a new one; --atomic rolls back by itself when an upgrade fails.

choices.label: Fix the broken resources by hand with kubectl
choices.feedback: Search works, but Helm's record no longer matches the cluster, and the next upgrade will fight your edits.

choices.label: helm uninstall search and install it fresh
choices.feedback: Uninstall deletes the release's resources, including its index volume claim; search is down and its index must be rebuilt.

reflection.question: Write the release record: how the catalog and search were recovered, and what keeps the next release from taking them down.

scoring.modelReasoning: A Deployment keeps a revision history: kubectl rollout status shows progress, and rollout undo returns to a known-good revision without deleting anything. The strategy decides capacity during a rollout: maxUnavailable 0 with a surge means readiness gates every step, while maxUnavailable 100% or Recreate removes every serving Pod first. Helm keeps release revisions too: helm rollback restores one, --atomic undoes a failed upgrade, and uninstall deletes the release's resources.
